title: CourseSource
description: A course's sources (courses/<id>/course.yaml and units/; docs/migration-design.md, deliverable 1): its course.yaml and units, pointing at its language's lexicon.

orthographies.description: Orthographies the course teaches; the first is the default. Learners may switch (§6.3, apc).

names.description: What the app calls the course and its orthographies, in the support language at least (ADR 0109; lint course.names).

license.description: Default SPDX license for every content item that gives none.

provenance.description: Default provenance for every content item that gives none.

facets.description: The facets the course practises (§8.5, ADR 0071); by default all of them. Exercises of any other facet are never planned: a course for a written language leaves out listen and speak, and one that shows its readings without drilling them leaves out read-script.

consistentReadings.description: Every reading in the course is fixed by its word's spelling, sense, form and morphs (ADR 0135): words annotated alike that read two ways (a scheme's reading, or the vowel marks a vocalization gives) are an error, `reading.inconsistent`, where a course without it gets the warning `reading.inconsistent-pending`. A token marked `readingVariant` is left out. Switched on once the course is clean.

wordParts.description: The course asks words by their parts (ADR 0152): a lesson may ask a word built from its parts (`parts-whole`: its own word and the form or morphs it carries, typed) and a word's parts picked out (`whole-parts`). Off unless set: a course switches it on once the parts its tokens carry (`form`, `morphs`) have been checked.

iPlusOne.description: Maximum new knowledge components per sentence (§7.5). Default 1.

oneOf.description: Path to a unit file, relative to course.yaml.

vocalization.description: Vowel marks for the course's words, by orthography (ADR 0053): a file next to course.yaml, or given inline. The compiler marks every word of sentences, stories and word forms with them, so the vowel-marks toggle has something to show.

lexicon.description: The language whose lexicon the course draws on (lexicons/<lang>/).

own.title: OwnLexicon
own.description: The lexicon of a course kept in one file (a test's fixture, an imported course, a draft): its language's lexicon and declaration written here, which the compiler then reads instead of lexicons/<lang>/. A course of the repo has none: a language's lexicon is its courses' together, never one course's.

variety.description: The variety the course teaches, one of its language's (ADR 0145: an utterance has one). Dialect tags on prompts are derived from it (ADR 0147).

registers.description: The registers the course teaches, of its language's.

UnitSource.title: UnitSource

title.description: Per support language (the key is a support orthography's language, e.g. en).

stories.description: Stories (gameplan §8.2 `story`, Phase 6): dialogue to read, each on a path node of kind story.

graphemes.description: The letters this unit's script nodes teach (ADR 0149: a grapheme stays the script track's, never the lexicon's).

UnitSource.description: A unit of a course (docs/migration-design.md). It defines no lexemes: its nodes point at the language's lexicon, so a unit can be rearranged without touching it. The letters its script nodes teach are the one thing it still lists.

GraphemeSource.title: GraphemeSource
GraphemeSource.description: A letter, a digraph or a mark a script track teaches: what a grapheme KC was.

forms.description: How it is written, per orthography: a letter's forms, and in a Latin orthography what a script track asks it as (ADR 0133).

alphabet.description: script nodes that teach an orthography from scratch (ADR 0088): lexemes for reading and writing practice, each one whose citation form the letters taught by this node and the ones before it spell.

convert.description: script nodes: convert sentences between two orthographies (script-convert, §6.3).

forms.description: The sentence in each orthography of the course.

translations.description: Accept sets per support language (key: the support orthography's language, e.g. en). The first alternative is the displayed translation.

production.description: Used for L1→L2 production (needs `reverse` in every form). Default true.

uses.description: What the sentence is an example of beyond its tokens' lexemes: a rule, or a listed item with slots (what a `construction:` KC became; ADR 0145). Until rules are written the compiler cannot find these itself.

tags.description: What the answer must say and the prompt leaves open (ADR 0147), shown under the prompt where the answer's language marks it. A dialect tag is derived by the compiler from the course's variety and is never written here.

PromptTag.title: PromptTag
PromptTag.description: One tag (ADR 0147): a value from a closed set, rendered from the UI catalog (persons, register), or an authored situation in each support language. Exactly one of the three.

situation.description: By support language: "it (the school)", "(every day)". It names the situation, never the grammar, and never shows the answer's form.

SentenceForm.title: SentenceForm
SentenceForm.description: The exact surface text, plus tokens that annotate it in order. Gaps between tokens become space and punctuation tokens.

reverse.description: Target-language accept set (§7.4) for L1→L2 production.

SourceToken.title: SourceToken
SourceToken.description: A token: a stretch of text, with the lexemes it writes. There is no unit between a token and a lexeme (the owner, 2026-11-20: no `word` inside): a stem, a clitic and an affix are all lexemes the token writes. One that writes a single lexeme names it itself (`lexeme`, `feats`); one that writes several lists them (`lexemes`). Never both.

lexeme.description: The one lexeme the token writes.

feats.description: The feature values chosen here, never the lexeme's own lexical features (mano's gender is its entry's).

lexemes.description: The lexemes the token writes, in the order it writes them (apc b + el + matbakh; uz uy + ga).

n.description: Its number among the lexemes the utterance writes, from 1, in order. Written where a relation names it or it names one.

head.description: The `n` of the lexeme it agrees with or is governed by (ADR 0145: only where agreement or government matters; a full tree comes with the first rule that needs one).

tile.description: Tile group. Default: each token that writes a lexeme is its own tile.

vocalized.description: This token's vowel-marked form (ADR 0053), where its surface is a homograph the course's vocalization file lists as ambiguous. Its marks removed, it must equal the surface.

context.description: A context that changes how the word is said but not how it is written or what it is (ADR 0135), as the source's accents encode it where the course's text leaves them out: Biblical Hebrew `pause` (a clause's last word, its stress moved: ʾānṓḵî) and `nesiga` (stress drawn back before a stressed syllable: qā́rāʾ láylâ). Words in different contexts may read differently; the reading check compares each context apart.

readingVariant.description: Its reading is a free variant of the form's (ADR 0135): the reading check (`reading.inconsistent`) leaves it out, and it is never filled in from another token. Only where nothing in the sentence decides the reading.

TokenLexeme.title: TokenLexeme
TokenLexeme.description: One lexeme of a token that writes several.

surface.description: Its letters in the token. Empty for one the script does not write, or writes only as a mark on a letter it shares (ADR 0136: the ezafe).

base.description: The lexeme the token's others are merged onto (ADR 0145: every complex form is a base lexeme merged with another, one head per step): matbakh in b + el + matbakh, uy in uy + ga. It is what a question about the token asks (which lexeme, which form) and where its feature values are chosen. At most one; a token of two equals has none (yue 十 + 八).

n.description: Its number among the lexemes the utterance writes, from 1, in order. Written where a relation names it or it names one.

head.description: The `n` of the lexeme it agrees with or is governed by (ADR 0145: only where agreement or government matters; a full tree comes with the first rule that needs one).

StorySource.title: StorySource
StorySource.description: A short story: lines of dialogue or narration, read in the learner's orthography, with questions along the way. A tap glosses a token from the lexemes it writes.

node.description: The path node (kind story) the story is read at.

title.description: The title per support language (key: e.g. en).

StoryStep.title: StoryStep
StoryStep.description: One step of a story: a line, or a comprehension question.

speaker.description: A character id; none for narration.

forms.description: The line in every orthography of the course, tokenized like a sentence's forms.

translations.description: The line's meaning per support language: shown on request, never graded.

ask.description: Ask before showing the line. complete: choose what is missing at `gap`; arrange: build the line from its tiles, given its translation.

gap.description: The lexeme the line leaves out and asks for.

distractors.description: complete. asks lexeme: other lexemes, each shown as the course writes it in the gap's form (a token of the story's unit or an earlier one that writes that lexeme with the gap's feature values; story.distractor-form where there is none). asks form: other feature values, each shown as the gap's lexeme in the attested form that has them; left out, the compiler chooses two attested forms.

items.description: Another lexeme (which lexeme); another form of the gap's own, as its feature values (which form); or a word built of several lexemes, as a token of the course writes them in that order (apc esm and its ending, where the gap is one word too).

CourseAudio.title: CourseAudio
CourseAudio.description: How the course gets audio (gameplan §10): synthesized from pinned readings by the listed voices, or recorded by people only. Audio belongs to the language, not an orthography: each voice reads one orthography's forms.

humanRequired.description: Refuse synthesis: only human recordings (dialects and languages without good TTS, §10.1).

quality.description: How far learners may rely on the course's clips (ADR 0091). good (the default): clips play everywhere, listening and listen-and-repeat exercises included. iffy: a stopgap voice, often right but not always; its clips only reinforce what the learner reads (after a card is answered, in stories, in the word list), and no exercise depends on hearing them. bad: no clip reaches the learner; the clips stay in the course's audio folder for reviewers and the audio check.

AudioVoice.title: AudioVoice
AudioVoice.description: A synthetic voice of the course's cast.

speaker.description: Whose voice it is: a man's (m) or a woman's (f). A course's voices share its items at random; a sentence or story character whose grammar says who speaks goes to a voice of that gender, if the cast has one (ADR 0078). A cast of one voice reads everything.

voice.description: The provider's voice: an eSpeak NG voice name, a Piper voice id (or, with `model`, the voice's file stem in that repo), an ElevenLabs voice_id, a Cartesia voice id, or for OmniVoice, Navoiy and VoxCPM2 a reference voice the audio index holds (`nabu audio cast`), whose voice every clip clones.

model.description: Hosted providers: the model, pinned to a dated snapshot where the provider has one (Cartesia "sonic-3.6-2026-08-27"; ElevenLabs "eleven_v4"). OmniVoice, Navoiy, VoxCPM2, and a Piper voice outside rhasspy/piper-voices: the Hugging Face checkpoint and its commit ("openbmb/VoxCPM2@…", "MahtaFetrat/Mana-Persian-Piper@ad9dd851…", "oddadmix/lahgtna-omnivoice-v2@55c38a61…", "aisha-org/navoiy-tts@9445f41e…"). It is the clips' recorded version.

language.description: The language code the provider takes for this course (ElevenLabs language_code, Cartesia language, OmniVoice language id), e.g. "fa", "uz", "yue", "ar". The Lahgtna checkpoint's dialect ids reuse country codes: "lb" is Lebanese Arabic there.

vowelMarks.description: With reading "text": read the text with the vowel marks the course's vocalization gives (ADR 0053) rather than as the source writes it, for a voice whose model reads them (Lahgtna reads تشكيل). A change to the vocalization then changes the clips it touches.

finalStop.description: End text that has no final punctuation (word cards, mostly) with the full stop of its script ("." in Latin, Cyrillic and Arabic script, "。" in Han, "।" in Devanagari; ADR 0063); with a phoneme reading (tiberian, attic), end the phonemes with "." (ADR 0089). Voices say a lone word more naturally as a sentence. Turning it on makes the clips it touches stale.

pronounce.description: With reading "text": a reading scheme pinned on tokens ("jyutping"). A token whose spelling does not settle its pinned reading (a polyphone, or a reading the character table lacks) is given to the provider as IPA instead of its spelling. Needs a provider that reads inline IPA (elevenlabs).

spoken.description: What the voice reads instead of an item's text (item id: text in the orthography), for a reading the text does not settle: a homograph (نه is noh "nine" in the numbers drill, na "no" elsewhere: drill.numbers.9: نُه). Vowel marks where they settle it. It must have as many words as the item, so word timings still map. The full stop of `finalStop` is added after it.

reading.description: What the voice reads: "text" (the orthography's form) or a reading scheme pinned on tokens ("jyutping").

license.description: License of the audio this voice produces: it follows the voice's own terms.

AudioCarrier.title: AudioCarrier
AudioCarrier.description: Piper: an item of at most `maxWords` words (word cards, mostly) is said at the end of this sentence and cut out at its first frame, its phonemes given at least the frames the carrier's phonemes get (ADR 0065). Some Piper models garble a lone word: their durations collapse and their reading of a short input is off, while sentences are fine. VoxCPM2: an item without closing punctuation (a word card) is said after this text, with the script's full stop, and cut out by forced alignment (ADR 0094); `maxWords` is not used.

text.description: The carrier, in the voice's orthography, ending where the item begins ("حالا این کلمه را تکرار کن، ": "now repeat this word, …").

maxWords.description: The longest item the carrier says, in words: its word tokens, so a script written without spaces counts too.

AudioPace.title: AudioPace
AudioPace.description: VoxCPM2: a sentence the voice says faster than `target` syllables (Han characters) a second is slowed toward it with Rubber Band, pitch and formants kept, by at most `maxStretch` (ADR 0094). A learner's normal pace, not the player's slow speed (ADR 0062). Word cards are cut from the carrier as they are.

maxStretch.description: The most a clip is made longer (1.6: 60% longer).

DrillSpec.title: DrillSpec
DrillSpec.description: A generated drill family (§7.6). numbers: cardinals spelled out with CLDR RBNF.

ScenarioSource.title: ScenarioSource
ScenarioSource.description: A roleplay scenario card (gameplan §13.4): who the model plays and what the learner tries to do. The model writes every line at run time, inside the learner's known vocabulary; the card holds no target-language text.

after.description: The path node a learner completes before the scenario opens.

setting.description: Where the conversation happens, per support language. Shown to the learner and sent to the model.

character.description: Who the model plays, per support language.

goal.description: What the learner tries to do, per support language.

speaker.description: The character's gender as a speaker, where the course sets it: a man (m) or a woman (f). Its lines go to a voice of the cast that matches (ADR 0078); without it, the character gets a voice of the cast at random, the same for every line of the story.

name.description: The name as written in each orthography of the course (keys: orthography ids).

StoryChoiceSource.title: StoryChoiceSource
StoryChoiceSource.description: A comprehension question in the support language, about what has been read.

VocalizationSource.title: VocalizationSource
VocalizationSource.description: A course's vowel marks for one orthography (ADR 0053): each word's vocalized form. A surface with several pronunciations is ambiguous: each of its tokens names its own (SourceToken.vocalized).

words.description: Surface → vocalized form (its marks removed, it is the surface).

ambiguous.description: Surfaces with more than one vocalization in the course: each token chooses.

uncertain.description: Surfaces the drafter was unsure of: a reviewer checks these first.
